question.prompt: Find the square roots and the principal square root of 9. (Answer in this order: first write the two square roots of 9, with the positive one first and the negative one second, then write the principal square root of 9. Separate the answers with commas.)

solutions.explanation: Because \(3^2=9\) and \((-3)^2=9\), the square roots of 9 are \(\pm3\). The positive square root, 3, is the principal square root.
solutions.title: Use the square-root definitions
